We can make a static index.html and ideally modular JS/CSS. Need a quality game. Let's think about gameplay.

2D dirtbike wheelie game:
- Side-view dirtbike, physics wheelie balance.
- Goal: hold wheelie as long as possible, score based on angle and time, avoid looping over (crash beyond ~110 degrees) and keep bike moving.
- Controls: throttle (ArrowUp / W / right touch), lean back/forward (left/right or A/D), brake maybe.
- Button to change dirtbike (cycle through 3-4 bikes with different colors/stats).
- Complete playable with start screen, HUD, score, combo, best, particles, terrain parallax, sound maybe WebAudio engine.
- Mobile responsive touch controls.
- Need no external assets ideally, draw everything canvas with procedurally generated bike art.

Could do a polished neon/sunset desert vibe. Canvas with crisp pixel-ish or vector style.

Mechanics details:
Let's define bike physics.

Simplified wheelie model:
- bike has position x at rear wheel contact? Better: treat bike as rigid body with two wheels on ground, angle theta (pitch, positive = front raised/back wheel down). To make fun and controllable, use a hybrid arcade model:
  - Speed increases with throttle, decreases with drag/brake.
  - Wheelie angle from balance: gravity torque pulls front down (towards 0); throttle torque lifts front. Lean input adds torque.
  - If angle > 0, front wheel lifted. Balance point around 45-55 degrees? Actually a wheelie balance point is around 60-90 deg relative horizontal. Bike angle drawn rotation around rear wheel.
  - Use angle in degrees 0..120. Throttle gives lift torque; gravity pulls down. At high speed maybe more stable.
  - Lean back / forward adjust torque.
  - Ground contact: at angle ~0 front wheel touches. Rear wheel always contact.
  - Wheelie score multiplier when angle > threshold (say 18 deg), combo grows until 100 deg danger zone.
  - If angle > 105, crash (loop out). If angle returns below 5 maybe wheelie ends, but no crash.
  - Need to maintain speed/throttle. Add "balance" physics with oscillation? For skill, gravity torque is max near 90 (unstable). Let's model inverted pendulum: gravity torque = g * sin(angle) pulling back down (toward 0) for small angle? An inverted pendulum tips away from 0, but a bike wheelie with rear wheel drive: gravity torque tips it over backwards once past balance. Hmm. Better arcade: torque_g = k * sin(theta) pushing back toward 0; then throttle lifts, and player modulates. This creates equilibrium at angle where throttle torque = gravity torque. To sustain high angle, need more throttle, but throttle also increases speed. At balance angle around 45 deg equilibrium. Player can hold.

But if gravity always restoring, then wheelie naturally falls unless throttle. Fun.

Angle dynamics:
theta (radians, >=0).
angular velocity w.
Torque = liftTorque * throttle - gravityTorque * sin(theta) - damping*w + leanTorque.
Where liftTorque maybe 9 rad/s², gravityTorque ~ 7.5. Equilibrium sin(theta)=9/7.5 >1 impossible if full throttle. Hmm need equilibrium at high angle if gravity torque peaks. Set gravity max at theta=90? sin works; equilibrium sin = lift/gravity. If lift=6, gravity=7.5 => theta=53° at full throttle. Good. But to reach >100 impossible without lean? Player lean adds torque, allow up to 105. Use lean back extra torque.

Maybe two-part: throttle torque ~5, gravity ~6, lean back adds ±4. Equilibrium at full throttle + full lean back impossible, causing loop out. So player holds near.

Let's simulate: throttle torque T=8, gravity=10*sin theta, balance at sin=0.8 => 53°. If lean back +3 => sin=1.1 impossible -> accelerates over. If lean forward -3 => sin=0.5 => 30°. So to cruise 60-80, feather throttle and lean. This could be fun but maybe too twitchy.

Could instead make gravity torque small restoring and angle is controlled mostly by throttle. Let's tune with easy mode. Also if angle < 0, clamp 0 with slight bounce.

Speed: throttle accelerates; if angle high, acceleration reduced? Rear wheel power causes lift. Let's have speed target ~ [0, 260] px/s. World scroll to right; background moves.

Actually for score, keep bike x fixed-ish around 30% screen and scroll terrain? Easier: bike moves right in world; camera follows. Ground is generated with gentle hills. Visual scrolling speed = speed. Score from distance + wheelie time.

Need terrain to add slopes affecting angle? Simpler flat ground, parallax and road markings. Could add jump ramps? Not necessary. Keep flat with small bumps visual.

Let's design game loop:
- states: menu, playing, crashed.
- Start screen with title "WHEELIE RIDER", bike preview, controls, start button.
- HUD top left: score, best, speed, angle, combo/wheelie time, balance meter.
- On-screen buttons: gas at bottom right, brake bottom left, lean buttons? Mobile touch: gas and lean back/forward. "change bike" button in HUD top right always available, including during play (switches bike instantly, minor burst effect).
- Keyboard: Up/W throttle, Down/S brake, Left/Right lean. Space restart/start. B cycle bike.
- Mouse/touch: buttons.
- Bike switch changes appearance and stats: e.g. 3 bikes:
  1. "MudMuncher 250" balanced, red/white.
  2. "Neon Hornet" lighter, more flickable, faster lift but twitchier.
  3. "Torque Titan" heavier, stable, more grip lower lift.
  Perhaps 4th "Sandstorm" vintage.
  Differences in physics: power, lift, stability, mass.
- Show bike name and stat bars in switch toast.

Visual:
- Canvas responsive with devicePixelRatio, centered.
- Background: sunset gradient sky, sun, layered mountains, clouds, desert/track parallax, ground with speed streaks, dust particles from rear wheel.
- Bike: draw vector shapes with suspension, wheels with spokes rotating, rider with helmet and lean pose, exhaust smoke. Lean shifts rider.
- Rear wheel at pivot; front wheel position rotates around rear. Draw bike in local coordinates rotated by theta around rear wheel contact. Actually physics angle = bike's pitch, pivot at rear axle. Render rear wheel at (x, groundY - wheelR) and rotate all bike parts around rear axle by -? For front lift, rotate counter-clockwise (negative canvas angle).
- Ground contact for rear wheel. Draw wheel center at rear axle, with bike body rotated.
- Add rider animated arms/legs.
- Dust particles when throttle on ground; front wheel spray when wheelie.
- Screen shake on crash? maybe.
- Sound: WebAudio engine hum with oscillator, changes pitch with speed/throttle; optional mute button. Use no external assets. Need user gesture to start AudioContext. Add mute toggle.
- High score localStorage.
- Pause when tab hidden.
- Crash: if angle > 110 or speed drops to 0 while wheelie? Crash loop out animation: bike tumbles. "WIPEOUT" overlay with score and restart button.
- Combo: wheelie score accumulates faster at higher angle with risk; zone meter.

Could make the game a single index.html with inline CSS and JS? Better split into index.html, style.css, game.js for maintainability. Static server supports.
